judgment.reasoning: An established roster requirement was violated

notApplicable.reason: The SDK composes no elicitation requests of its own: CreateElicitationRequest.form/url are factories the application calls with its own content (AcpSchema.java:2462-2481) and the only main-source path is the pass-through at agent/DefaultAcpAsyncAgent.java:248-261, so the condition "the SDK itself composes elicitation requests" does not hold.
Same: the SDK never decides what to elicit or in which mode; it only transmits the application's request (agent/DefaultAcpAsyncAgent.java:248-261; AcpSchema.java:2462-2481).

observations.message: DefaultInitialize never advertises sessionCapabilities.additionalDirectories (null at agent/DefaultInitialize.java:43); a builder agent needs its own initialize handler for it, while the annotated path can advertise it (AgentAdvertisement.java:313).

The prose lists MCP servers as required while protocol-conformance/spec/official/agent-client-protocol/schema/v1/schema.json requires only sessionId and cwd for ResumeSessionRequest; the SDK follows the schema (AcpSchema.java:1526).

The check is skipped while no initialize request has been recorded (caps == null at agent/DefaultAcpAsyncAgent.java:306-307), so a client call issued before initialize, for example from an extension handler, is sent unchecked.

`providers` and `fork` are not properties of the stable schema's AgentCapabilities/SessionCapabilities; a builder agent that registers provider or fork handlers writes them at the root of those stable types (agent/DefaultInitialize.java:43, 48-51).
CreateElicitationRequest has fixed components and no any-setter (AcpSchema.java:2439-2444), so mode-specific fields of a custom mode are dropped on read rather than preserved for proxying.

The mode-specific requireds (requestedSchema for form; elicitationId and url for url) are @Nullable on the flattened record (AcpSchema.java:2442-2443), so RequiredFields does not reject a received form request that lacks requestedSchema.
The client's raw requestHandler/notificationHandler accept any non-typed method name, underscore or not (client/AcpClient.java:564-593), intended for protocol methods the SDK does not model.
